evidence.observation: createFileRoutes owns the acceptance contract for user-controlled attachment metadata: it registers GET /api/chat/generated-file and, in order, normalizes the client-supplied path query value (line 37 via the imported normalizeGeneratedFileRequestPath), rejects an empty or NUL-byte result with 400 (51-54), resolves the candidate against the realpath'd workspace (line 74 via resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath), rejects anything escaping the workspace and everything on the denylist with 403 (96-102, denylist call at line 98), rejects non-regular files and oversized files with 400/413 (104-116), and finally echoes file metadata name/path/size/mimeType parsed from the resolved real path back to the client (120-130, MIME parse at line 128). The inline helpers this route used to define are now imported from ../utils/generated-file-metadata.js (lines 6-10); the route itself and its call sites are unchanged.

The 100 MiB attachment size cap for the generated-file download contract is declared once here and enforced in the route at lines 113-115 (413 'File is too large to download'); the surrounding lines 31-32 document that the user-controlled path/metadata rules were moved to ../utils/generated-file-metadata.js so they can be unit tested.

Pure normalizer for the user-controlled path: strips trailing slashes from the workspace realpath, folds backslashes to '/', and classifies the request as 'workspace-absolute' only when the requested value equals the workspace or starts with '<workspace>/'; every other value is re-anchored under the workspace (leading slashes stripped) and reported as 'workspace-root-relative' or 'workspace-relative'. This is why a look-alike sibling workspace such as /home/wattman/.wattclaw/user/report-agent-evil is never treated as absolute by the handler, and is the function the new test suite drives.

Parses/normalizes the user-controlled path query value: non-string input collapses to '' (so the route answers 400) and strings are trimmed then have '\' folded to '/' before any path resolution. This is the exact expression the handler used inline before extraction (files.js:37), so empty/whitespace-only and Windows-separator requests behave identically.

Case-insensitive policy normalizer over the workspace-relative path: it lowercases the path segments, denies any segment in GENERATED_FILE_DENIED_SEGMENTS (.git, .openclaw) and denies the basenames .env, .env.* and the agent-instruction/state files listed in GENERATED_FILE_DENIED_NAMES (agents.md, soul.md, user.md, identity.md, tools.md, bootstrap.md, memory.md, workspace-state.json, openclaw-workspace-state.json). Moved verbatim from files.js, where it is the 403 decision at line 98.

Attachment-metadata parser: takes the last extension via path.extname, lowercases it, and maps it through GENERATED_FILE_MIME_TYPES (pdf/doc/docx/xls/xlsx/ppt/pptx/csv/txt/md/json/zip/png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/svg), falling back to application/octet-stream for unknown or missing extensions. This value is what the handler advertises as file.mimeType at files.js:128.

The new focused test suite's fixture harness: it replays the handler's ordered decision chain (normalize -> 400 guard -> resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath -> workspace-containment check -> isGeneratedFilePathAllowed -> attachment metadata) for each user-controlled fixture, with posix.relative standing in for the realpath round trip. The 13 node:test cases below it cover separator/trim normalization, non-string values, NUL bytes, pathMode classification, sibling-workspace re-anchoring, the exported denylist constants, accepted vs denied attachment names (case variants), the traversal-vs-denylist layering, MIME parsing, and the composed end-to-end fixture table.

The executable demo's fixture list of user-controlled attachment paths (root-relative, Windows separators with padding, workspace-absolute, sibling look-alike, traversal, .git, AGENTS.md, .env, non-string). Running `node server/utils/generated-file-metadata.demo.mjs` prints the normalized operation result for each fixture; the recorded output is reproduced in .prale-eval/contract-deliverable.md.

The repository test entry point now runs the new focused suite with the built-in runner, in the same `node --test --test-force-exit` invocation that already runs the dependency-free server/services/external-session-projection.test.js suite, so the parser/normalizer test is part of `npm run test:server` in a fully installed checkout.

claims.claim: The user-controlled `path` query value of generated-file downloads is parsed and normalized before any filesystem access: non-string values collapse to '', strings are trimmed and Windows separators are folded to '/', and the empty / NUL-byte result is rejected with 400.

After normalization the request is anchored under the workspace realpath: only a path equal to or below the workspace is honoured as workspace-absolute, while look-alike sibling workspaces and UNC-style inputs are re-anchored inside the workspace, so the user-controlled value can never address a path outside the workspace root.

Attachment access is then decided by two distinct layers: a workspace-containment check on posix.relative(workspaceReal, targetReal) (403) and a case-insensitive denylist rejecting .git/.openclaw segments plus .env*/.env-style secrets and agent-instruction/state files by basename; the denylist alone is not a traversal boundary (../outside.txt passes it and is stopped by containment).

The metadata answered to the client for an accepted attachment is derived from the resolved real path: name = basename, path = workspace-relative posix path, mimeType = lowercased extension lookup with unknown or missing extensions mapped to application/octet-stream, and files above the 100 MiB GENERATED_FILE_MAX_BYTES cap are rejected with 413.

The extraction of the parser/normalizer helpers out of server/handlers/files.js into server/utils/generated-file-metadata.js is behaviour-preserving: the new module and the previous inline implementations produce identical outputs across the checked MIME/extension corpus and relative-path corpus used for validation.

A focused, dependency-free parser/normalizer suite for these user-controlled fixtures now exists and passes: 13 node:test cases driven by fixture tables, runnable via `node --test server/utils/generated-file-metadata.test.js`, wired into `npm run test:server`, and accompanied by an executable demo that prints the normalized operation result.

conclusion: The task is delivered as a focused parser/normalizer test for user-controlled generated-file (chat attachment) request metadata. The previously inline normalizers in server/handlers/files.js (request-path normalization, workspace-relative path policy/denylist, extension-to-MIME parsing) were extracted into the dependency-free server/utils/generated-file-metadata.js, which the route now imports with identical behaviour, and a new fixture-driven node:test suite (server/utils/generated-file-metadata.test.js) exercises the full contract together with the existing resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath normalizer in server/utils/generated-file-path.js. All 13 tests pass in this checkout via `node --test`, the executable demo reproduces the normalized operation results, and the extraction was verified equivalent to the pre-change inline code over 26 MIME/extension inputs and 13 relative paths with zero differences. No task metadata, hidden-oracle file, package lock or git configuration was touched.
